evaluation: Scripts without arg declarations retain preparation-time expression evaluation. Declared arguments create a bounded typed program evaluated for each invocation with fresh immutable bindings. All branch names and types are validated before activation.
authoringRules: Match the feature ID to the filename.
Keep the command name unique among active features.
Write each statement on its own line and delimit blocks with braces.
Keep permission nodes explicit and preserve them when editing message text.
Use quoted text, integer literals or booleans. Local types are inferred and bindings are immutable.
Check both branches for type errors. Use text(value) for explicit conversion.
Validate the complete edited source before requesting a local reload.
statements: arg name: text | integer | boolean [= constantExpression]

operations.permissions: declared command permission on invocation and before each action
operations.errors: Static scripts validate emitted text during preparation. Runtime argument programs validate argument values and prepare all messages before emitting them.

editExample.expectedChange: Only the greeting changes. Feature ID, permission and sender remain the same.

runtimeArguments.ordering: Declare arguments first in the command block. Required arguments precede defaults. Values bind positionally.

types.text: Plain text supplied as one value
types.integer: Signed 64-bit decimal, with an optional + or - sign

runtimeArguments.failure: Missing, extra or invalid arguments reject invocation before any message is emitted. Arithmetic and output errors include source locations.
